name: Urgency & Distraction
description: Urgency bypasses deliberate thinking. When a target believes a situation is time-critical — a server is down, an inspection is running behind, a fire alarm test must happen now — they are less likely to follow verification procedures and more likely to grant access immediately. Distraction techniques occupy the attention of security personnel while a confederate performs the operational objective. Both are most effective when combined with a strong pretext and authority framing.

blue.det: Employee reports being pressured to bypass normal process; security staff notices rushed or agitated visitor; post-incident review reveals process was bypassed.
blue.cm: Written policy that urgency never overrides verification; security awareness training on urgency exploitation; slow-down protocol for any request bypassing normal process.
